bc_j_undertow.blurb: Undertow is a small bouldering zone in Squamish, tucked into the Grand Wall Boulders at the foot of the Stawamus Chief. It has six problems, and the spread is wide for such a compact spot: a couple of beginner-level lines near the bottom, a few mid-range problems around V4, and then a steep jump to a V7 and a V9 at the top end. It suits a climber who has already warmed up elsewhere on the Grand Wall trail and wants a handful of well-regarded problems in one place, with a couple of easier ones to start on.

bc_yosemite_boulder.blurb: Yosemite Boulder sits in the Pemberton Boulders zone, north of Whistler along the Sea to Sky corridor. It holds six problems on a single block, covering nearly the full range from V0 up to V8, so it works for a mixed group. Most of the interest is in the middle: a V3 face that is rated among the best of its grade in the corridor, plus a V4 and a couple of strong lines at the harder end. The block is a short walk from the parking area, behind a larger neighbouring boulder, and is a good stop within a longer Pemberton bouldering day.

bc_g_milf.blurb: G-Milf is a compact bouldering spot in the Silver Lake zone of the Fraser Valley, beside the river. It has only six problems, and they lean hard: one around V4, a pair near V7, and the remainder in the V9 to V11 range, so this is a place for strong boulderers rather than newcomers. The lines are short, powerful and technical, with a seated start on the hardest one. Bring a couple of pads, as the ground around the boulders is uneven.

_expect.name: South & West Faces (from Adamant or AusterityGlacier)

bc_3_south_west_faces_from_adamant_or_au.blurb: These are the big south and west walls of the Adamant group in the northern Selkirks, plus the north face of Blackfriars. There are six alpine and trad climbs, running from 5.8 up to 5.11, mostly multi-pitch and serious in character. Parties usually set up camp on the Adamant or Austerity glacier and work through the routes from left to right across the walls. The terrain is remote, with most teams flown in by helicopter from Golden. Expect glacier travel and snow couloirs alongside the rock climbing, which makes this a committed alpine objective rather than a day at the crag.
